description: The dotnet CLI's solution, reference, format and template commands, and C# file-based apps, with asm projects among .NET ones: a classic .sln made, filled (a solution folder too), listed, built, trimmed and migrated to .slnx; dotnet reference add between two asm projects, list and remove; dotnet format of a solution it can only partly read; dotnet run of a file-based app whose #:project is an .asmproj; and the templates' list, details and dry run.

steps.description: A classic .sln, the format dotnet new sln makes only when asked since .NET 10.

steps.run: dotnet sln Classic.sln add Lib/Lib.asmproj Prog/Prog.asmproj
steps.description: dotnet sln add writes an .asmproj with the SDK's generic project type.

steps.run: dotnet sln Classic.sln add Shared/Shared.asmproj --solution-folder natives

steps.description: dotnet reference add takes an .asmproj into an .asmproj (into a .csproj it still refuses one: PlugAndPlay).
The .sln builds every project for this machine, the program linking the static library the reference brings.
mul_ints(6, 7) through the reference dotnet reference add wrote.
The .sln becomes a .slnx that keeps the asm projects' type and the solution folder.
dotnet format checks the C# projects and skips the asm ones (Roslyn reads no .asmproj), and the solution as a whole passes.
A file-based app's #:project directive takes an .asmproj: the library is built for this machine and the app gets its binding.
And builds the same way without running.
The templates under test, into this scenario's own CLI home.
A dry run says what it would create and creates nothing.
